verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              युधिष्ठिरेणैवमुक्तः कौन्तेयः श्वेतवाहनः । असिं जग्राह संक्रुद्धो जिघांसुर्भरतर्षभम् ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Hearing the words of Yudhishthira, Kownteya-the owner of white steeds-in a tempestuous mood took hold of his sword to slay that mightiest of the Bharata's race.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य कोपं समुद्वीक्ष्य चित्तज्ञः केशवस्तदा । उवाच किमिदं पार्थ गृहीतः खड्ग इत्युत ॥२॥
verses.english: Kesava, the cogniser of human hearts, seeing his rage, inquired-"Why, O Partha, do you lay your hands on your sword?
verses.bhavadeepa: युधिष्ठिरेणेति ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: न हि पश्यामि योद्धव्यं त्वया किञ्चिद्धनञ्जय । ते ग्रस्ता धार्तराष्ट्रा हि भीमसेनेन धीमता ॥३॥
verses.english: Here, O Dhananjaya, I see no adversary to try the strength of your steel. Clever Bhimasena has already assailed the Dhartarashtras.

verses.sanskrit: अपयातोऽसि कौन्तेय राजा द्रष्टव्य इत्यपि । स राजा भवता दृष्टः कुशली च युधिष्ठिरः ॥४॥
verses.english: O Kownteya, you have returned from the field, to seen king Yudhishthira and you have seen that he is keeping up well.

verses.sanskrit: स दृष्ट्वा नृपशार्दूलं शार्दूलसमविक्रमम् । हर्षकाले च संप्राप्ते किमिदं मोहकारितम् ॥५॥
verses.english: This is the time of rejoicing, as you have seen that best of kings whose prowess is like that of a tiger. Why should you then betray yourself thus?

verses.sanskrit: न तं पश्यामि कौन्तेय यस्ते वध्यो भविष्यति । प्रहर्तुमिच्छसे कस्मात्किं वा ते चित्तविभ्रमः ॥६॥
verses.english: O son of Kunti, I do not find any one here whom you can slay. What makes you then to yearn for fight, or have you lost the balance of your mind?

verses.sanskrit: कस्माद्भवान्महाखड्गं परिगृह्णाति सत्वरः । तत्त्वां पृच्छामि कौन्तेय किमिदं ते चिकीर्षितम् ॥७॥
verses.english: Why do you seize your mighty sword so suddenly, I enquire this of you. O Kaunteya, whence is this desire of your heart, or why do you fly to sword in such a sullen mood and with such a vigour?"

verses.sanskrit: परामृशसि यत्क्रुद्धः खड्गमद्भुतविक्रम । एवमुक्तस्तु कृष्णेन प्रेक्षमाणो युधिष्ठिरम् ॥८॥
verses.english: Thus addressed by Krishna, Arjuna, looking towards Yudhishthira and whizzing like an angry snake, replied,

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुनः प्राह गोविन्दं क्रुद्धः सर्प इव श्वसन् । अन्यस्मै देहि गाण्डीवमिति मां योऽभिचोदयेत् ॥९॥
verses.english: He who tells me-'Give your Gandiva to another,' I would cut his head off, such is my secret vow. Now that this king of immeasurable prowess has told me those words in your presence, O Govinda, I won't forgive him. I will, therefore, put to the sword this pious king.

verses.sanskrit: भिन्द्यामहं तस्य शिर इत्युपांशुव्रतं मम । तदुक्तं मम चानेन राज्ञाऽमितपराक्रम ॥१०॥
समक्षं तव गोविन्द न तत्क्षन्तुमिहोत्सहे । तस्मादेनं वधिष्यामि राजानं धर्मभीरुकम् ॥११॥
प्रतिज्ञां पालयिष्यामि हत्वैनं नरसत्तमम् । एतदर्थं मया खड्गो गृहीतो यदुनन्दन ॥१२॥
verses.english: I will redeem my vow by slaying this best of men. For this alone I have taken up the sword.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽहं युधिष्ठिरं हत्वा सत्यस्यानृण्यतां गतः । विशोको विज्वरश्चापि भविष्यामि जनार्दन ॥१३॥
verses.english: O delighter of the Yadus; by slaying Yudhishthira I will thus adhere to truth thereby be free from grief and fever.

verses.sanskrit: किं वा त्वं मन्यसे प्राप्तमस्मिन्काल उपस्थिते । त्वमस्य जगतस्तात वेत्थ सर्वं गतागतम् ॥१४॥
verses.english: O Janaradana, what do you wish me to do under the present circumstances. O sire, you are well acquainted with all the past the future of this universe. I shall, therefore, do as you tell me.”

verses.sanskrit:
तत्तथा प्रकरिष्यामि यथा मां वक्ष्यते भवान् । सञ्जय उवाच।
              धिग्धिगित्येव गोविन्दः पार्थमुक्त्वाब्रवीत्पुनः ॥१५॥

कृष्ण उवाच।
              'इदानीं पार्थ जानामि न वृद्धाः सेवितास्त्वया । काले न पुरुषव्याघ्र संरंभं यद्भवानगात् ॥१६॥
verses.english: “Now I understand, O Partha, that you have never attended upon the old, since you, O mightiest of men, have been overcome with anger at a time quite out of season.

verses.sanskrit: न हि धर्मविभागज्ञः कुर्यादेवं धनञ्जय । यथा त्वं पाण्डवाद्येह धर्मभीरुरपण्डितः ॥१७॥
verses.english: O Dhananjaya, those who are versed in the niceties of religion would never act in the way as you are doing today, O pious son of Pandu, on not being acquainted with them.
verses.bhavadeepa: भवान्यत्संरम्भम् अगात् तत्काले न अकाले इत्यर्थः ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: अकार्याणां क्रियाणां च संयोगं यः करोति वै । कार्याणामक्रियाणां च स पार्थ पुरुषाधमः ॥१८॥
verses.english: O Partha, he who does an act improper and heinous is the vilest of men.

verses.sanskrit: अनुसृत्य तु ये धर्मं कथयेयुरुपस्थिताः । समासविस्तरविदां न तेषां वेत्सि निश्चयम् ॥१९॥
verses.english: You know not the words of wisdom the learned men preach, after the rules of morality, to the pupils waiting up on them.
verses.bhavadeepa: कर्तुमयोग्यानां कर्मणां संयोगं कर्तुं योग्यानामपि अक्रियाणां निषिद्धक्रियाणां संयोगं यः करोति स पुरुषाधम इत्याह - अकार्याणामिति ॥१८॥

verses.sanskrit: अनिश्चयज्ञो हि नरः कार्याकार्यविनिश्चये । अवशो मुह्यते पार्थ यथा त्वं मूढ एव तु ॥२०॥
verses.english: Persons ignorant of them become benumbed and befooled in discriminating between what ought to be done and what ought not, even as you, O Partha, have been nonplussed.
verses.bhavadeepa: उपस्थिताः शिष्यैरनुसृताः गुरवः ॥१९॥

verses.sanskrit: न हि कार्यमकार्यं वा सुखं ज्ञातुं कथंचन । श्रुतेन ज्ञायते सर्वं तच्च त्वं नावबुध्यसे ॥२१॥
verses.english: 'It is not easy to learn what ought to be done and what ought not. Of course everything can be learnt with the help of the scriptures. You are, however, a stranger to them.

verses.sanskrit: अविज्ञानाद्भवान्यच्च धर्मं रक्षति धर्मवित् । प्राणिनां त्वं वधं पार्थ धार्मिको नावबुध्यसे ॥२२॥
verses.english: Believing yourself to be conversant with morality, you are observing it in a way which but indicates your ignorance of it. You believe yourself to be virtuous but you know not, O Partha, that it is a sin to slay living beings.
verses.bhavadeepa: सुखम् अनधीत्येत्यर्थः । श्रुतेन शास्त्रेण ॥२१॥

verses.sanskrit: प्राणिनामवधस्तात सर्वज्यायान्मतो मम । अनृतां वा वदेद्वाचं न तु हिंस्यात्कथञ्चन ॥२३॥
verses.english: Methinks, keeping from doing any injury to any animal is a cardinal virtue. Even an untruth might behold but never an animal ought be slain.
verses.bhavadeepa: यत् भवान् धर्मं रक्षति तदवज्ञानात् अधर्ममेव धर्मं मनुषे इत्यर्थः । यतः प्राणिनां वधं दोषकरं इत्येतन्नावबुध्यसे ॥२२॥

verses.sanskrit: स कथं भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठं राजानं धर्मकोविदम् । हन्याद्भवान्नरश्रेष्ठ प्राकृतोऽन्यः पुमानिव ॥२४॥
verses.english: O best of men, how could you then like an ordinary man wish to slay your eldest brother the king, who is well versed in morality.

verses.sanskrit: अयुध्यमानस्य वधस्तथाऽशत्रोश्च मानद । पराङ्मुखस्य द्रवतः शरणं चापि गच्छतः ॥२५॥
verses.english: O Bharata, the slaying of a man who is not engaged in a fight, or is unwilling to fight, or takes to flight, or seeks your shelter, or joins his hands, or gives himself up to you, or is insane, be he even a foe, is never upheld by the righteous. And your superior is even all this.

verses.sanskrit: कृताञ्जलेः प्रपन्नस्य प्रमत्तस्य तथैव च । न वधः पूज्यते सद्भिस्तच्च सर्वं गुरौ तव ॥२६॥
verses.bhavadeepa: अशत्रोः अशातनीयस्य अवध्यस्य ॥२५॥

verses.sanskrit: त्वया चैवं व्रतं पार्थ बालेनेव कृतं पुरा । तस्मादधर्मसंयुक्तं मौर्ख्यात्कर्म व्यवस्यसि ॥२७॥
verses.english: You had formerly taken the vow through childishness. And now through folly you are inclined to do an unrighteous act.

verses.sanskrit: स गुरुं पार्थ कस्मात्त्वं हन्तुकामोऽभिधावसि । असंप्रधार्य धर्माणां गतिं सूक्ष्मां दुरत्ययाम् ॥२८॥
verses.english: Why, O Partha, do you rush upon your superior, intending to slay him, without determining (before-hand) the exceedingly fine course of virtue which is, certainly, not easily intelligible.

verses.sanskrit: इदं धर्मरहस्यं च तव वक्ष्यामि पाण्डव । यद्ब्रूयात्तव भीष्मो हि पाण्डवो वा युधिष्ठिरः ॥२९॥
verses.english: O son of Pandu, this mystery of virtue I will now explain to you as it was explained by Bhishma, by the pious Yudhishthira, by Vidura or the so-called Kshatri and by Kunti of great renown. I will tell it you in all its detail; listen to it, O Dhananjaya.

verses.sanskrit: विदुरो वा तथा क्षत्ता कुन्ती वाऽपि यशस्विनी । तत् ते वक्ष्यामि तत्त्वेन निबोधैतद्धनञ्जय ॥३०॥
सत्यस्य वदिता साधुर्न सत्याद्विद्यते परम् । तत्त्वेनैव सुदुर्ज्ञेयं पश्य सत्यमनुष्ठितम् ॥३१॥
verses.english: One who tells the truth is a pious person. Nothing is there higher than truth. It is, therefore, very difficult to understand the details of truth as observed in action.

verses.sanskrit: भवेत्सत्यमवक्तव्यं वक्तव्यमनृतं भवेत् । यत्रानृतं भवेत्सत्यं सत्यं चाप्यनृतं भवेत् ॥३२॥
verses.english: Truth becomes unutterable and untruth utterable, where untruth would pose as truth and truth as untruth.
verses.bhavadeepa: सत्यं तत्त्वेन याथातथ्येन सुदुर्ज्ञेयं पश्य । क्वचित्सत्यमप्यधर्माय भवतीत्यर्थः ॥३१॥

verses.sanskrit: विवाहकाले रतिसंप्रयोगे प्राणात्यये सर्वधनापहारे । विप्रस्य चार्थे ह्यनृतं वदेत पञ्चानृतान्याहुरपातकानि ॥३३॥
verses.english: At a marriage or in the enjoyment of lust, or when one's life is at stake, or when one's entire fortunes are about to be lost, or in the cause of a Brahmin untruth may be uttered. It is said that there is no sin in uttering these five sorts of falsehood.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वस्वस्यापहारे तु वक्तव्यमनृतं भवेत् । तत्रानृतं भवेत्सत्यं सत्यं चाप्यनृतं भवेत् । तादृशं पश्यते बालो यस्य सत्यमनुष्ठितम् ॥३४॥
verses.english: Where one's entire fortunes are at stake untruth becomes utterable. On these occasions untruth becomes truth and truth untruth. He who is bent upon always practising truth alone is a fool and takes truth to be as it is.

verses.sanskrit: भवेत्सत्यमवक्तव्यं न वक्तव्यमनुष्ठितम् । सत्यानृते विनिश्चित्य ततो भवति धर्मवित् ॥३५॥
verses.english: Indeed it is not a very easy thing to become righteous. He who can distinguish between the niceties of truth and untruth can alone become conversant with morality.
verses.bhavadeepa: यस्य येन हेतुना सत्यमेव सत्यतया अनुष्ठितं तादृशमेव पश्यति सत्यवादितया अनेन हेतुना बालः अज्ञः ॥३४॥

verses.sanskrit: किमाश्चर्यं कृतप्रज्ञः पुरुषोऽपि सुदारुणः । सुमहत्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यं बलाकोऽन्धवधादिव ॥३६॥
verses.english: What wonder is there then that a wise man by doing something awfully cruel may even acquire virtue, as Balaka did by killing a blind beast.

verses.sanskrit: किमाश्चर्यं पुनर्मूढो धर्मकामो ह्यपण्डितः । सुमहत्प्राप्नुयात्पापमापगास्विव कौशिकः' ॥३७॥
verses.english: What wonder then that an ignorant and inexperienced person, intending to practise virtue, would commit grave vice like Kaushika on the river-bank."

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच।
              आचक्ष्व भगवन्नेतद्यथा विन्दाम्यहं तथा । बलाकस्यानुसंबन्धं नदीनां कौशिकस्य च ॥३८॥
verses.english: Arjuna said Tell me of it, O holy one, in a way that I may learn it these stories about Balaka and Kaushika on the river-bank.

verses.sanskrit:
वासुदेव उवाच।
              'पुरा व्याधोऽभवत्कश्चिद्बलाको नाम भारत । यात्रार्थं पुत्रदारस्य मृगान् हन्ति न कामतः ॥३९॥
verses.english: Vasudeva said There was once a hunter, O Bharata, Balaka by name. He used to kill animals, not willfully but, in order to support his children and wife.

verses.sanskrit: वृद्धौ च मातापितरौ बिभर्त्यन्यांश्च संश्रितान् । स्वधर्मनिरतो नित्यं सत्यवागनसूयकः ॥४०॥
verses.english: Devoted to his tribal pursuits, always speaking the truth and devoid of malice, he used to maintain his aged mother and father and other dependents.

verses.sanskrit: स कदाचिन्मृगं लिप्सुर्नाभ्यविन्दन्मृगं क्वचित् । अपः पिबन्तं ददृशे श्वापदं घ्राणचक्षुषम् ॥४१॥
verses.english: Once on a day, thought diligently searching for an animal, he could find none. At last he found a beast of prey, drinking water, which had lost its eyes but the loss was supplied by its keen sense of smell.

verses.sanskrit: अदृष्टपूर्वमपि तत्सत्त्वं तेन हतं तदा । अन्धे हते ततो व्योम्नः पुष्पवर्षं पपात च ॥४२॥
verses.english: Though he had not before seen a like of it, yet he killed it then and there. No sooner the blind beast had been killed, that there fell from the skies a shower of flowers.

verses.sanskrit: अप्सरोगीतवादित्रैर्नादितं च मनोरमम् ।   विमानमगमत्स्वर्गान्मृगव्याधनिनीषया ॥४३॥
verses.english: A celestial car, filled with the songs and music of Apsaras, came down from heaven to fetch that hunter of animals.

verses.sanskrit: तद्भूतं सर्वभूतानामभावाय किलार्जुन । तपस्तप्त्वा वरं प्राप्तं कृतमन्धं स्वयंभुवा ॥४४॥
verses.english: That beast having, successfully performed all the austerities of asceticism with a view to kill all the animals, had received that boon but was made blind instead by the Self-born.

verses.sanskrit: तद्धत्वा सर्वभूतानामभावकृतनिश्चयम् । ततो बलाकः स्वरगादेवं धर्मः सुदुर्विदः ॥४५॥
verses.english: Therefore Valaka, having killed the beast that was bent upon killing all the animals, went to heaven. Morality is, therefore, very difficult to be understood.

verses.sanskrit: कौशिकोऽप्यभवद्विप्रस्तपस्वीनो बहुश्रुतः । नदीनां सङ्गमे ग्रामाददूरात्स किलावसत् ॥४६॥
verses.english: There was an ascetic Brahmin named Kaushika not much read in the Scriptures. He used to reside at a confluence of rivers, not far away from a village.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यं मया सदा वाच्यमिति तस्याभवद्व्रतम् । सत्यवादीति विख्यातः स तदाऽसीद्धनञ्जय ॥४७॥
verses.english: He had taken the vow that the would ever speak the truth.' Therefore, O Dhananjaya, he become famous as a truthful man.
verses.bhavadeepa: तपस्विनः तपस्विनामिनः श्रेष्ठः ॥४६॥

verses.sanskrit: अथ दस्युभयात्केचित्तदा तद्वनमाविशन् । तत्रापि दस्यवः क्रुद्धास्तानमार्गन्त यत्नतः ॥४८॥
verses.english: At a time certain persons, being afraid of robbers, entered the woods. Even there the robbers, filled with anger, doggedly haunted after them.

verses.sanskrit: अथ कौशिकमभ्येत्य प्राहुस्ते सत्यवादिनम् । कतमेन पथा याता भगवन्बहवो जनाः ॥४९॥
verses.english: They then approaching Kaushika the truthful, said-'O holy one, which way have a number of men passed a little while ago? Asked in the name of truth tell us if you have seen them.'

verses.sanskrit: सत्येन पृष्टः प्रब्रूहि यदि तान् वेत्थ शंस नः । स पृष्टः कौशिकः सत्यं वचनं तानुवाच ह ॥५०॥
बहुवृक्षलतागुल्ममेतद्वनमुपाश्रिताः । इति तान् ख्यापयामास तेभ्यस्तत्त्वं स कौशिकः ॥५१॥
verses.english: Being thus asked Kaushika told them the truth, that they had entered the wood thickly covered with trees, creepers and shrubs. O Partha, thus did Kaushika inform them.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्ते तान्समासाद्य क्रूरा जघ्नुरिति श्रुतिः । तेनाधर्मेण महता वाग्दुरुक्तेन कौशिकः ॥५२॥
verses.english: And the report goes that on this those wanton men got hold of those persons and put them to death. For the gave sin of uttering that truth, which should not have been uttered, Kaushika, unversed in the subtleties of religion, fell into a fearful hell.

verses.sanskrit: गतः स कष्टं नरकं सूक्ष्मधर्मेष्वकोविदः । यथा चाल्पश्रुतो मूढो धर्माणामविभागवित् ॥५३॥
verses.english: As a foolish man, ill-read in the scriptures, unacquainted with the details of morality, is fit to fall into an awful hell for not asking aged men to set his doubts at rest.

verses.sanskrit: वृद्धानपृष्ट्वा सन्देहं महछ्वभ्रमिवार्हति । तत्र ते लक्षणोद्देशः कश्चिदेवं भविष्यति ॥५४॥
verses.english: Your definition of morality must be then something like that. Some people attempt at attaining that high and difficult knowledge by the exercise of reasoning. Many persons maintain, on the other hand, that morality can be learned from the scriptures alone.

verses.sanskrit: दुष्करं परमं ज्ञानं तर्केणानुव्यवस्यति । श्रुतेर्धर्म इति ह्येके वदन्ति बहवो जनाः ॥५५॥
verses.bhavadeepa: श्वभ्रमिव नरकमिव अपृष्ट्वा प्रश्नमकृत्वार्हति तत्र धर्माधर्मयोस्तत्त्वे निश्चेतव्ये लक्षणस्य उद्देशः- वचनं भविष्यति ॥५४॥

verses.sanskrit: तत्ते न प्रत्यसूयामि न च सर्वं विधीयते । प्रभवार्थाय भूतानां धर्मप्रवचनं कृतम् ॥५६॥
verses.english: I do not find fault with the latter, but then everything is not provided for there. The moral precepts have been made for the well-being of the creatures.
verses.bhavadeepa: क्वचित्तर्केणापि धर्मस्वरूपं निर्णेयमित्याह- दुष्करमिति ॥५५॥

verses.sanskrit: यत्स्यादहिंसासंयुक्तं स धर्म इति निश्चयः । अहिंसार्थाय हिंस्त्राणां धर्मप्रवचनं कृतम् ॥५७॥
verses.english: All that is free from any motive of injury to any being is surely morality. For, indeed, the moral precepts have been made to free the creatures from all injuries.
verses.bhavadeepa: न प्रत्यसूयामि न दूषयामि अनुमानतोऽपि धर्मो ज्ञेय इत्याशयेनाह- न चेति । लक्षणोद्देशमाह- प्रभवेति ॥५६॥

verses.sanskrit: धारणाद्धर्ममित्याहुर्धर्मो धारयते प्रजाः । यत्स्याद्धारणसंयुक्तं स धर्म इति निश्चयः ॥५८॥
verses.english: Dharma (morality) is so-called because it protects all. Indeed, morality saves all creatures. Surely then that is morality which is capable of keeping off a creature from all injuries.
verses.bhavadeepa: अहिंसैव धारणाद्धर्म इत्याह- हिंसार्थायेति ॥५७॥

verses.sanskrit: येऽन्यायेन जिहीर्षन्तो धर्ममिच्छन्ति कर्हिचित् । अकूजनेन मोक्षं वा नानुकूजेत्कथञ्चन ॥५९॥
verses.english: Those who try to stick to them logically, have scarcely a mind to acquire morality. If you can get rid of them without a word do no account have any intercourse with them.

verses.sanskrit: अवश्यं कूजितव्ये वा शंकेरन्नप्यकूजतः । श्रेयस्तत्रानृतं वक्तुं तत्सत्यमविचारितम् ॥६०॥
verses.english: If he must be spoken to or if he takes offence on not being talked with, in that case better speak a falsehood; verily that untruth is truth.
verses.bhavadeepa: न्यायेन ‘सन्तोषं जनयेत्प्राज्ञस्तदेवेश्वरपूजनम्’ इत्यादिवाक्यावष्टम्भेन अन्योन्यसुखहेतुत्वात्पारदार्यादिकमपि धर्म इति वदन्तो धर्मापहारमिच्छन्ति ते अकूजनेन वेदशब्दराहित्येन तद्विरुद्धं धर्मं मोक्षं वा वेदबाह्यमिच्छन्ति तान्प्रति नानुकूजेत् तैः सह संवादमपि न कुर्यादसंभाष्यास्ते तेन वेदाविरोधे सति यदन्यस्य सुखकरं तद्धर्म इत्यर्थः ॥५९॥

verses.sanskrit: यः कार्येभ्यो व्रतं कृत्वा तस्य नानोपपादयेत् । न तत्फलमवाप्नोति एवमाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥६१॥
verses.english: He who, having taken a vow on some set purpose, cannot redeem the same by acts, attains not the rewards of that vow.
verses.bhavadeepa: यत्र तु धर्मसन्देहे वेदशब्दो नास्ति नापि लौकिकी युक्तिरस्ति । तत्र किं कर्तव्यमित्याशङ्क्याह - अवश्यमिति । यत्र ब्राह्मणः स्तेनत्वेन ज्ञातः तत्रेतरेषां स्तेनोऽयमस्ति नो वेति संशये पक्षद्वयेऽपि हिंसाप्राप्तौ मौनमेवाश्रयेत् । मौनेनाप्यसिद्धौ अनृतमपि वदेदित्यर्थः ॥६०॥

verses.sanskrit: प्राणात्यये विवाहे वा सर्वज्ञातिवधात्यये । नर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्ते वा न च प्रोक्तं मृषा भवेत् ॥६२॥
verses.english: When one's life is endangered, at marriage, at the risk of destruction of one's kith and kin or in the course of business, all that is uttered will not be regarded as falsehood. To those who are well-versed in the real secrets of morality, there appear no immorality in all this.
verses.bhavadeepa: य इति । कार्येभ्यः यत्किञ्चित्कार्यं मनस्युद्दिश्य व्रतं कृत्वा तस्य व्रतस्य नाना अन्येन प्रकारेणोपपादनं करोति स दाम्भिको व्रतफलं नाप्नोतीत्यर्थः ॥६१॥

verses.sanskrit: अधर्मं नात्र पश्यन्ति धर्मतत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः । यः स्तेनैः सह संबंधान्मुच्यते शपथैरपि ॥६३॥
श्रेयस्तत्रानृतं वक्तुं तत्सत्यमविचारितम् । न च तेभ्यो धनं देयं शक्ये सति कथञ्चन ॥६४॥
verses.english: On no account should one's wealth he give to the robbers, if that could be helped. Wealth when give to the sinful afflicts even the donor.

verses.sanskrit: पापेभ्यो हि धनं दत्तं दातारमपि पीडयेत् । तस्माद्धर्मार्थमनृतमुक्त्वा नानृतभाग्भवेत् ॥६५॥
verses.bhavadeepa: तेभ्यः स्तेनेभ्यः ॥६४॥

verses.sanskrit: एष ते लक्षणोद्देशो मयोद्दिष्टो यथाविधि । यथाधर्मं यथाबुद्धि मयाद्य वै हितार्थिना ॥६६॥
verses.english: Therefore, an untruth spoken in the cause of morality does not amount to a falsehood. I have now duly pointed out to you the distinctive feathers of morality. Having heard all these tell me, O Partha, if Yudhishthira deserves to be killed.
verses.bhavadeepa: पीडयेत् नरकं प्रापयेत् ॥६५॥

verses.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा ब्रूहि पार्थ यदि वध्यो युधिष्ठिरः । अर्जुन उवाच।
              यथा ब्रूयान्महाप्राज्ञो यथा ब्रूयान्महामतिः ॥६७॥
हितं चैव यथाऽस्माकं तथैतद्वचनं तव । भवान्मातृसमोऽस्माकं तथा पितृसमोऽपि च ॥६८॥
verses.english: Arjuna said "O Krishna! You have spoken as a man of great wisdom should say, as a man of great intelligence need say. Your words are even such as would do good to us.

verses.sanskrit: गतिश्च परमा कृष्ण त्वमेव च परायणम् । न हि ते त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यतेऽविदितं क्वचित् ॥६९॥
verses.english: You are like both a mother and a father to us. You, O Krishna, are our sanctuary; that is why your words are beneficial to us.

verses.sanskrit: तस्माद्भवान्परं धर्मं वेद सर्वं यथातथम् । अवध्यं पाण्डवं मन्ये धर्मराजं युधिष्ठिरम् ॥७०॥
verses.english: Nothing is there in the three worlds that is unknown to you. Therefore, you know the sublime morality with all its niceties.
verses.bhavadeepa: अविदितमिति च्छेदः ॥६९॥

verses.sanskrit: अस्मिंस्तु मम संकल्पे ब्रूहि किंचिदनुग्रहम् । इदं वा परमत्रैव शृणु हृत्स्थं विवक्षितम् ॥७१॥
verses.english: I admit that the righteous Yudhishthira, son of Pandu, is unslayable. In this connection kindly tell me something in my favour. Hear me tell you of something else that lies in my heart.

verses.sanskrit: जानासि दाशार्ह मम व्रतं त्वं यो मां ब्रूयात्कश्चन मानुषेषु । अन्यस्मै त्वं गाण्डिवं देहि पार्थ त्वत्तोऽस्त्रैर्वा वीर्यतो वा विशिष्टः ॥७२॥
verses.english: You know, O Keshava, the best scion of the Dasharha race, that my vow is that whoever among men tells me 'make over, O Partha, your Gandiva to him who is superior to you in point of chivalry or in wielding armours' I will, with all my mighty, slay him. So Bhima also has taken a vow to slay the man who addresses him as 'one without the hirsute indications of manhood!' Just now the king has repeatedly told me in your presence “make over your bow.
verses.bhavadeepa: अनुग्रहम् अवधेन प्रतिज्ञारक्षणम् ॥७१॥

verses.sanskrit: हन्यामहं केशव तं प्रसह्य भीमो हन्यात्तूबरकेति चोक्तः । तन्मे राजा प्रोक्तवांस्ते समक्षं धनुर्देहीत्यसकृद्वृष्णिवीर ॥७३॥
तं हन्यां चेत्केशव जीवलोके स्थाता नाहं कालमप्यल्पमात्रम् । ध्यात्वा नूनं ह्येनसा चापि मुक्तो वधं राज्ञो भ्रष्टवीर्यो विचेताः ॥७४॥
verses.english: O Keshava, if I slay him, surely then the thought of having slain the king will immerse me in sin and make me loose my valour and mental faculties and thus cut short my days in this world.
verses.bhavadeepa: तूबरकः बहुभोजनः ॥७३॥

verses.sanskrit: यथा प्रतिज्ञा मम लोकबुद्धौ भवेत्सत्या धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठ । यथा जीवेत् पाण्डवोऽहं च कृष्ण तथा बुद्धिं दातुमप्यर्हसि त्वम् ॥७५॥
verses.english: Therefore, O Krishna, the best of all the righteous inen, do give me such counsels as would uphold my well-known vow and leave both myself and the eldest son of Pandu alive."
verses.bhavadeepa: तं हन्यामिति । स्थाता न - न स्थास्ये एनसा मुक्तोऽपि कृतप्रायश्चित्तोऽपि न स्थास्ये इत्यर्थः । किं कृत्वा राज्ञो वधं ध्यात्वा ॥७४॥

verses.sanskrit:
वासुदेव उवाच।
              राजा श्रान्तो विक्षतो दुःखितश्च कर्णेन संख्ये निशितैर्बाणसङ्घैः । यश्चानिशं सूतपुत्रेण वीर शरैर्भृशं ताडितो युध्यमानः ॥७६॥
verses.english: Vasudeva said-"O valiant one, the King Yudhishthira feels weary and aggrieved on being afflicted with arrows shot at him by Karna during the campaign; the more so as he was harassed with shaft-shots by the son of Suta even when he was retiring form the field.

verses.sanskrit: अतस्त्वमेतेन सरोषमुक्तो दुःखान्वितेनेदमयुक्त रूपम् । अकोपितो ह्येष यदि स्म संख्ये कर्णं न हन्यादिति चाब्रवीत्सः ॥७७॥
verses.english: Heavy at heart as he was at all this, he used such angry and improper expressions to you. Moreover, he addressed you in that tenor thinking that if he could provoke you, you would forthwith slay Karna in battle.

verses.sanskrit: जानाति तं पाण्डव एष चापि पापं लोके कर्णमसह्यमन्यैः । ततस्त्वमुक्तो भृशरोषितेन राज्ञा समक्षं परुषाणि पार्थ ॥७८॥
verses.english: O Partha, the king believes that this immoral Karna is unbearable to everyone else on earth but you. It was this that enraged him so highly as to use such cruel words even in your face.

verses.sanskrit: नित्योद्युक्ते सततं चाप्रसह्ये कर्णे द्यूतं ह्यद्य रणे निबद्धम् । तस्मिन् हते कुरवो निर्जिताः स्युरेवं बुद्धिः पार्थिवे धर्मपुत्रे ॥७९॥
verses.english: King Yudhishthira, the righteous, is of opinion that today's battle is a play at dice in which the life of the ever-deviceful and everover bearing Karna has been laid as an wager. If he is slain, the Kauravas would necessarily meet with defeat.

verses.sanskrit: ततो वधं नार्हति धर्मपुत्रस्त्वया प्रतिज्ञाऽर्जुन पालनीया । जीवन्नयं येन मृतो भवेद्धि तन्मे निबोधेह तवानुरूपम् ॥८०॥
verses.english: Therefore, O Arjuna, the son of Dharma deserves not death at your hands. At the same time your vow also must be kept good. Under the circumstances listen to the means that will make him apparently dead without the real loss of life.
verses.bhavadeepa: समक्षम् आवयोरिति शेषः ॥७८॥ कर्णे पणीकृते द्यूतं युद्धरूपम् ॥७९॥

verses.sanskrit: यदा मानं लभते माननार्हस्तदा स वै जीवति जीवलोके । यदाऽवमानं लभते महान्तं तदा जीवन्मृत इत्युच्यते सः ॥८१॥
verses.english: A man of honour lives in this material world so long as he receives the homage due to him, but when he is woefully dishonored, he is spoken of as one more dead than alive.

verses.sanskrit: संमानितः पार्थिवोऽयं सदैव त्वया च भीमेन तथा यमाभ्याम् । वृद्धैश्च लोके पुरुषैश्च शूरैस्तस्यापमानं कलया प्रयुङ्क्ष्व ॥८२॥
verses.english: O Partha, this king has ever been honored by you, Bhima and the twins and by all the wise and chivalrous men to this world. You just offer some insult to that king.

verses.sanskrit: त्वमित्यत्रभवन्तं हि ब्रूहि पार्थ युधिष्ठिरम् । त्वमित्युक्तो हि निहतो गुरुर्भवति भारत ॥८३॥
verses.english: O Bharata, a superior on being addressed as 'you' dies (at heart). Therefore, you do addressed the much-respected Yudhishthira as 'you.'

verses.sanskrit: एवमाचर कौन्तेय धर्मराजे युधिष्ठिरे । अधर्मयुक्तं संयोगं कुरुष्वैनं कुरूद्वह ॥८४॥
verses.english: O the best of Kurus, O son of Kunti, do behave thus towards Yudhishthira the righteous and insult that honorable man by this censurable behaviour.
verses.bhavadeepa: अत्रभवन्तं मान्यं त्वमिति ब्रूहि तावतैव तद्वधः कृतो भवतीत्यर्थः ॥८३॥

verses.sanskrit: अथर्वाङ्गिरसी ह्येषा श्रुतीनामुत्तमा श्रुतिः । अविचार्यैव कार्यैषा श्रेयस्कामैर्नरैः सदा ॥८५॥
verses.english: This is a Shruti given out by the Rishis Atharva and Angira, the best of all the Srutis; people who wish well should always follow this without any scruple.
verses.bhavadeepa: एवं पूज्यावमानरूपं संयोगम् आत्मनानुष्ठितं कुरुष्व ॥८४॥

verses.sanskrit: अवधेन वधः प्रोक्तो यद्गुरुस्त्वमिति प्रभुः । तद्ब्रूहि त्वं यन्मयोक्तं धर्मराजस्य धर्मवित् ॥८६॥
verses.english: To address a venerable superior as 'You.' is to kill him without actually depriving him of his life. Therefore do you, who are versed in morality, address Yudhishthira the righteous, in the manner I have indicated.
verses.bhavadeepa: तत्र मानमाह- अथर्वेति ॥८५॥

verses.sanskrit: वधं ह्ययं पाण्डव धर्मराजस्त्वत्तोऽयुक्तं वेत्स्यते चैवमेषः । ततोऽस्य पादावभिवाद्य पश्चात्समं ब्रूयाः सान्त्वयित्वा च पार्थम् ॥८७॥
verses.english: On your acting thus the righteous Yudhishthira will verily feel that you have offered him a death-blow. Later on you will worship his feet and speak to him in befitting terms and thus pacify him.
verses.bhavadeepa: यत् गुरुस्त्वमिति प्रोक्तस्तदवधेन शस्त्रपातनमन्तरेणैव वधः वधकरं भवतीत्यर्थः ॥८६॥

verses.sanskrit: भ्राता प्राज्ञस्तव कोपं न जातु कुर्याद्राजा धर्ममवेक्ष्य चापि । मुक्तोऽनृताद्भ्रातृवधाच्च पार्थ हृष्टः कर्णं त्वं जहि सूतपुत्रम् ॥८८॥
verses.english: O Partha, your intelligent brother Yudhishthira would never feel in the least angry with you. On being thus freed from impiety and fratricide you may cheerfully proceed against and slay Karna, the son of Suta.
verses.bhavadeepa: अयुक्तमेवं त्वत्तो वधं वेत्स्यते अनेनाहं हत इति ज्ञास्यतीत्यर्थः । समं वैषम्यपरिहारम् ॥८७॥
